clue.text: Love from scoundrel is hollow

indicators.note: taken from the run of words that follow, so the letters sit inside the text itself

parts.note: the letters run across the end of scoundrel, the whole of is and the start of hollow

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the affection shown by a rogue is empty and insincere.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is hidden across scoundREL IS Hollow; 'hollow' looks like the indicator but is just part of the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: To relish something is to enjoy it greatly, a verb synonym for adoring or taking great pleasure in it.

clue.text: Area in ether unusually warm again

indicators.note: one item placed in another means it goes inside the second word
done unusually means not in the normal order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
A is the standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A lab note: a region of ether, oddly, has warmed up a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To reheat food or a substance is to bring its temperature up once more after it has cooled.

clue.text: Decline to support useless person? Sweet

indicators.note: in a down clue one part supporting another sits underneath it, so it comes second

parts.note: a lemon is slang for a dud or a hopeless person
a decline or fall is a drop

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to back a hopeless friend, then shrugs: sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like a casual exclamation but is the definition, a British word for a piece of confectionery.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemon drop is a small boiled confectionery flavoured with citrus, which British speakers call a sweet.

clue.text: Grazed in fight before end, losing heart

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter of the word is dropped
one thing before another means it comes first in the line

parts.note: a scrap is a scuffle or brawl
taken as written before its middle goes

explanation.surface: A boxer picked up a graze in a bout just before the finish, having lost his nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: If skin is scraped it has been scratched raw by rubbing against something rough, like a graze.

clue.text: Disorder in retreat contained by skilful marshal

indicators.note: held inside the next word, which wraps around it

parts.note: able means competent or skilled

indicators.note: something in retreat goes backwards, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: a mess is a state of disorder

explanation.surface: A clever military commander keeps a disorderly retreat under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marshal' looks like a noun, the commander, but it is the verb meaning to gather together.
explanation.definitionFit: To marshal troops or facts is to gather and arrange them, just as one would collect them into a group.

clue.text: Hint on past got broadcast? Be ruthless

indicators.note: broadcast suggests scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, all thirteen letters

explanation.surface: A radio presenter is told a tip about history was aired: show no mercy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who will stop at nothing has no scruples or limits in pursuing a goal, which is ruthless behaviour.

clue.text: Carries out belongings

definitions.meaning: first meaning: brings about or implements, as a verb

explanation.surface: Someone removes their possessions, like a removal crew emptying a house.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as carrying belongings out of a house; split it into a verb phrase and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To effect a change is to bring it about, and a person's effects are the property they own.

clue.text: Restraint from cook about right

indicators.note: about means going around, so the first word encircles the second

parts.note: to bake is to cook in an oven
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A chef shows self-control in getting a dish just right.
explanation.definitionFit: A brake is a device or influence that checks motion or holds something back, a form of restraint.

clue.text: Put at risk, destroy bug

parts.note: to end something is to finish it off
to bug someone is to annoy or anger them

explanation.surface: Killing an insect could be dangerous, someone warns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' looks like an insect to be destroyed, but it is the verb meaning to irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger someone is to expose them to harm, the same as placing them in a hazardous position.

clue.text: Pal discarding clubs and diamonds? Odd routine

indicators.note: discarding a card means throwing it away, so a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a chum is a friend
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games, the letter removed
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games
rum is British slang for strange or odd

explanation.surface: A card player throws away clubs and diamonds, a dull and strange habit.
explanation.walkthrough: The clubs letter comes out of the friend; the diamonds letter then joins after, followed by rum, an old British word for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Humdrum describes something dull and lacking variety, as routine work is monotonous and ordinary.

clue.text: Good robot, see, working? It raises confidence

parts.note: moral means virtuous or good

indicators.note: working suggests being worked over or reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Look, the robot is functioning well again, which cheers the whole team.
explanation.definitionFit: A morale booster is anything that lifts spirits and self-belief, so it lifts people's assurance in themselves.

clue.text: Casual worker, bad at first

indicators.note: at first places this word at the start, ahead of the one before it

parts.note: food that has gone bad is off
a hand is a manual labourer, as in a farm hand

explanation.surface: A temporary employee performed poorly at the beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: An offhand manner is careless, relaxed and unceremonious, much like an informal or nonchalant attitude.

clue.text: Pavlova, say, almost immaculate, not available as part of range

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Anna Pavlova was a famous Russian ballerina, and say marks her first name as an example
pure means spotless, before its last letter goes
NA is the standard abbreviation for not available

explanation.surface: A meringue dessert, nearly perfect, has sold out from the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pavlova' suggests the dessert, but here it is the ballerina; the definition is a Himalayan peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Annapurna is a massif in the Himalayas of Nepal, one mountain within that great chain of peaks.

clue.text: Fair copy initially accompanied by spare

indicators.note: one part accompanied by another is followed by it in sequence
initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the first letter of copy
spare and lean both mean thin, without excess flesh

explanation.surface: A clean manuscript is handed in along with an extra copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair copy' reads as one phrase, a neat final version, but Fair is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean or fair fight is one played by the rules, and a fair copy is free of corrections.

clue.text: Cartoon character's not left friends in trouble

indicators.note: being in trouble means things are in disarray, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: the fodder, all fourteen letters

explanation.surface: An animated hero refuses to abandon his pals when they face danger.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the Stone Age family man at the centre of the animated sitcom The Flintstones.

clue.text: Running exercises covered by speech

indicators.note: covered by means wrapped inside the following word

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech, the outer part
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: A talk covers jogging and gym workouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' looks like jogging next to exercises, but it means the functioning of a machine or business.
explanation.definitionFit: The operation of a business or machine is how it works and is managed, its day-to-day functioning.

clue.text: Rapturous quote coming up about new cast

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means read from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards
about means surrounding, so the first part goes around the second

parts.note: to cite is to quote

indicators.note: a new version is a remade one, so the letters take a fresh order

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A director is overjoyed as a glowing review arrives for the new company of actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstatic means overwhelmed with joy or delight, the same state of bliss as being enraptured.

clue.text: Reliable element beginning to beat excessive protest back

parts.note: copper is a chemical element

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of beat
OTT is over the top, meaning excessive

indicators.note: going back means read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

explanation.surface: A chemist complains about overblown objections to their reliable metal.
explanation.walkthrough: Ships' hulls were once sheathed in copper for durability, hence the sense of thoroughly dependable.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper-bottomed means thoroughly safe and trustworthy, as in a guaranteed investment or a cast-iron promise.

clue.text: Former king after attention with story

indicators.note: after means this part follows the one named next in the line

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention
a story can be a falsehood, a lie
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An old monarch seeks an audience to tell his tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'king' tempts toward LEAR, but only the one-letter abbreviation is wanted, placed last.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier means previous or prior in time, so it can stand for former, as in an earlier version.

clue.text: Hunter mostly bearing north above Colorado river

indicators.note: in a down clue being above means coming earlier in the entry
bearing means carrying, so the shortened word holds the next letter inside it
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Orion is the hunter of Greek myth and the constellation
N is the abbreviation for north
CO is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Colorado

explanation.surface: A hunter heads north beyond the Colorado River.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing north' reads as a compass heading, but bearing means carrying: the clipped hunter holds the north letter. Colorado is only the abbreviation and river the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orinoco is one of the major South American rivers, flowing through Venezuela to the Atlantic.

clue.text: In hearing, stand by bias

indicators.note: in hearing means as perceived by the ear, so a word with a matching sound is wanted

parts.note: to stand by is to remain ready, to wait

explanation.surface: In a court hearing, a witness is asked to remain while partiality is considered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In hearing' suggests a court session, but signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Weight, in bowls, is a bias built into a ball; more generally it is a slant or influence tipping a balance.

clue.text: Member of dynasty bringing defeat about, seizing day

indicators.note: brought about means turned around, so the word runs backwards
seizing means grabbing hold of something and holding it within

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A royal house brings about a rival's defeat by taking the day.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the English royal family from Henry VII to Elizabeth I, so any one of them belongs to that line.

clue.text: Tense, like match going to penalties?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a game level after normal time, as in football when a shootout decides it

explanation.walkthrough: A football match that ends level goes to a penalty shootout, so it was tied; the question mark flags that this sense is indirect.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn face is strained with worry, while a drawn game ended with the scores equal.

clue.text: Found spirit with answer during old ceremony

indicators.note: during means within the span of the next part, so it sits inside it

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a rite is a ceremony
gin is a spirit
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Gin is discovered at an ancient ritual, along with a reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past tense of find; it is the verb meaning to set up, as in founding a company.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an institution is to establish it from scratch, which is to give rise to or begin it.

clue.text: Adherent of emperor in dire straits

indicators.note: something in a dire state is in a mess, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A loyal follower of a fallen Russian ruler finds himself in desperate trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in dire straits' reads as one idiom; 'in' is the link and 'dire' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarist supports the rule of a tsar, the title of the Russian emperor.

clue.text: Tips in general due to be favourable

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two ends, the first and final letters

parts.note: the outside letters of general
money that is due is owing

explanation.surface: Advice that, broadly speaking, one ought to be well disposed.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing review or report is full of praise, so it is highly positive and complimentary.

clue.text: Deception by artist in attempt to be perverse

indicators.note: by means placed next to, so the parts sit side by side

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle

indicators.note: in means placed inside the next word

parts.note: a try is an attempt, the outer part
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter's attempt at trickery is just awkward behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: A contrary person is stubbornly awkward and deliberately does the opposite of what is wanted, which is perverse.

clue.text: Poem shown in text at regular intervals

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means picking every other one

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and so on letters of these words

explanation.surface: A poem displayed periodically in a document.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonnet is a fourteen-line verse form, one particular kind of poem.
